engines.name: Electric motor (single-motor RWD or dual-motor AWD)

issues.t: Excessive oil consumption
issues.sym: The oil level drops quickly between changes, sometimes a quart or more every 1,000 to 2,000 miles. The low oil or oil pressure light may come on before the next service is due.
issues.why: Carbon can clog the oil control rings on the pistons of the 3.7L V6, so oil gets past the rings and burns in the cylinders. Acura issued service bulletins and a warranty extension on 2009-2014 vehicles with this engine.
issues.next: Check the dipstick every fill-up and keep the oil topped up, because running low can ruin the engine. Ask an Acura dealer to run an oil consumption test and check whether any extended coverage applies to your VIN.

issues.t: Leaking active dampers cause clunks and rough ride
issues.sym: Clunking or thumping over bumps, a bouncy or harsh ride, and less control on rough roads. You may see oily residue on the shocks, though the front units are mounted upside down and often hide the leak.
issues.why: The electronically controlled active dampers (shocks) can lose fluid, especially in cold climates. Acura extended the warranty on front and rear active dampers for 2010-2012 ZDX models, and those extensions have now expired.
issues.next: Have the dampers inspected if the ride changes or you hear clunks. Worn dampers hurt handling and braking, so replace them in pairs rather than waiting.

issues.t: Shudder between 20 and 60 mph
issues.sym: A vibration or shudder, like driving over rumble strips, during light acceleration or steady cruising between about 20 and 60 mph.
issues.why: The torque converter lock-up clutch can judder as it engages. Acura released a software update and later bulletins pointing to worn transmission fluid or a faulty torque converter.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check for the transmission software update and change the transmission fluid with genuine Acura fluid. If the shudder continues, the torque converter may need replacing.

issues.t: Front wheel bearing humming or moaning
issues.sym: A humming, droning or moaning sound from the front that rises with speed and may change when you steer left or right.
issues.why: Acura investigated front wheel bearing noise on 2011-2013 MDX and ZDX models. A worn bearing makes noise and gets worse over time.
issues.next: Have the front bearings checked. A noisy bearing can usually be driven on for a short time, but don't ignore it; a badly worn bearing can overheat or loosen the wheel.

issues.t: Low oil pressure light with correct oil level
issues.sym: The low oil pressure light flickers or comes on even though the dipstick shows the oil is full.
issues.why: Acura published service notes about this warning on 3.7L models. It can come from a sensor or wiring fault, but it can also be an early sign of low oil from consumption.
issues.next: Pull over and check the oil level right away. If the level is correct and the engine sounds normal, have a shop test actual oil pressure and the sensor before assuming it is a false warning.

issues.t: Low compression from out-of-round cylinders
issues.sym: Rough running, a misfire, a flashing or steady check engine light, and weak power.
issues.why: Acura issued a bulletin for some 2013 MDX, ZDX and TL engines whose cylinder bores were out of round, which causes low compression. The repair can require a new engine block.
issues.next: Have a compression test done if a misfire won't go away with new plugs or coils. Ask the dealer whether your engine falls under the bulletin.

issues.t: Check engine light for evaporative (EVAP) leak
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with no change in how the car drives. Codes such as P0455 or P0456 point to a fuel vapor leak.
issues.why: A loose or sticky fuel cap is the most common cause; Acura issued a bulletin on it. The EVAP canister vent solenoid can also stop working.
issues.next: Tighten or replace the fuel cap first, then clear the code. If it returns, have the EVAP system smoke-tested to find the leaking part.

issues.t: EGR valve failure
issues.sym: Check engine light, sometimes with rough idle, hesitation or pinging when accelerating.
issues.why: The exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) valve and its passages build up carbon until the valve sticks or the flow is blocked.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Cleaning the EGR passages and replacing the valve usually fixes it. Avoid hard driving if you hear pinging.

issues.t: Catalytic converter damaged by loose sensor cap
issues.sym: Check engine light for catalyst efficiency, a rattle from the exhaust near the engine, or a failed emissions test.
issues.why: Acura found that a cap on the air-fuel ratio sensor can come loose and damage the warm-up catalytic converter.
issues.next: If the converter code appears, ask the shop to look at the air-fuel sensor as well as the converter so the new part isn't damaged the same way.

issues.t: Won't move in Drive or Reverse after sitting overnight
issues.sym: The engine starts, but the car doesn't move when shifted into Drive or Reverse; pressing the gas only revs the engine. Moving the shifter between Park and Drive a few times gets it going.
issues.why: Owners report a delay in transmission engagement after the car sits. The exact cause has not been confirmed by Acura; low fluid pressure on start-up is a common reason for this kind of delay.
issues.next: Don't rev the engine while it fails to engage. Have the fluid level and condition checked and ask a dealer to scan the transmission for codes and updates.

issues.t: Loud exhaust from sticking muffler valve
issues.sym: The exhaust gets louder over time, especially on a cold start.
issues.why: A dealer traced this to a sticking valve inside the muffler that controls exhaust sound.
issues.next: Have the muffler checked. It is not a safety issue unless there is an actual leak, but a muffler replacement is the usual fix.

issues.t: Passenger airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. You may have received a recall letter.
issues.why: The Takata passenger front airbag inflator can break apart after years of heat and humidity and spray metal fragments in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls and book the free replacement with an Acura dealer right away.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. You may have received a recall letter.
issues.why: The original driver airbag inflator can absorb moisture and rupture, and some replacement inflators installed under earlier recalls were also defective.
issues.next: Look up your VIN for open recalls and have the free inflator replacement done, even if an earlier airbag recall was already completed.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may not open fully (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs.
issues.why: On some early 2010 ZDX models, the dashboard cover over the passenger airbag was not scored correctly, so the airbag might not deploy fully through it.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer inspects the dashboard cover and replaces it for free if needed.

issues.t: ABS releases brake pressure unexpectedly (recall)
issues.sym: While braking, the anti-lock brakes kick in when they shouldn't, and the car takes longer to stop than you expect.
issues.why: A software error in the brake control module on AWD models can activate ABS and release brake pressure. Acura recalled the car in 2024 and expanded the recall in late 2026.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and make sure the free brake software update (over the air or at a dealer) has been installed. Leave extra following distance until it is done.

issues.t: Front stabilizer bar bracket can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or rattle from the front passenger side. In the worst case the car loses drive power or shuts down.
issues.why: Bolts on the front passenger stabilizer bar bracket were not tightened properly at the factory. The loose bracket can damage high-voltage cables or battery coolant lines.
issues.next: Get the free recall inspection now. Dealers tighten the bolts and repair any damaged cables or coolant lines.

issues.t: Instrument display or backup camera goes blank (recall)
issues.sym: The driver display goes dark, so speed and warning lights are not shown, or the backup camera screen is blank in Reverse.
issues.why: Software errors in the radio control module can black out the instrument panel or the rearview camera image.
issues.next: Book the free software update at a dealer. Until then, be extra careful backing up and watch your speed by other means if the display fails.

issues.t: Rearview camera picture distorted or blank (recall)
issues.sym: The backup camera shows a distorted, frozen or blank image when you shift into Reverse.
issues.why: A faulty rearview camera can fail to send a clear image. Acura recalled the 2024 ZDX to replace the camera; owners report waiting for parts.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and ask the dealer when the replacement camera will be available. Use mirrors and look over your shoulder when reversing.

issues.t: Automatic emergency braking with nothing ahead
issues.sym: The car brakes hard on its own at city or highway speed, or while backing up, even though nothing is in the way.
issues.why: Owners report false activations of the forward collision and automatic braking system. It is the most common complaint filed with NHTSA for this car.
issues.next: Report each event to the dealer and to NHTSA, and ask about software updates. Keep sensors and the windshield camera area clean.

issues.t: Brake pedal sinks or Service Brake Assist warning
issues.sym: The brake pedal goes lower than normal, braking feels delayed, or a Service Brake Assist message appears, sometimes with a clicking feel at the pedal.
issues.why: The car uses an electronic brake system blended with regenerative braking. Owners report faults that dealers often cannot reproduce; related brake software has been recalled.
issues.next: Treat any brake warning seriously. Have the car checked by a dealer, make sure all brake software recalls are done, and don't drive it if the pedal goes to the floor.

issues.t: Infotainment, navigation or phone features stop working
issues.sym: The center screen, navigation, hands-free calling or the Acura app stop working, sometimes right after a software update.
issues.why: Software problems in the infotainment system and connected services are a repeated complaint.
issues.next: Try a restart of the system, then ask the dealer for the latest software. Keep notes of when it fails to help them diagnose it.

issues.t: Roof antenna cover comes loose
issues.sym: The shark-fin antenna on the roof rattles, lifts or comes off while driving or in a car wash.
issues.why: Owners report the antenna housing separating from the roof.
issues.next: If it is loose, have it secured before it falls off and lets water in. Ask the dealer to handle it under warranty.
